diagnosis: The scenario fails because the model can satisfy C1 and C6 using only shared information. Specifically, C1 (deciding to send a force-majeure notice) is satisfied by the mere existence of a force-majeure clause in the shared facts (S1/S2), and C6 (avoiding admission of liability) is satisfied by generic legal caution/standard business practice, even though PF3 contains specific policy terms regarding carrier notices.

C1.why: The shared record only establishes that a force-majeure clause exists; PF1 changes the decision to send the notice and sets the exact required method as both email and overnight courier.

C6.why: The policy terms are not in the shared record; PF3 changes the response to a carrier notice within exactly 10 calendar days, no admission of liability, and a carrier-notice commitment.
